chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, all from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:

Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) took the women with him in the war so that they would treat the wounded, and he did not distribute to them anything from the war booty, but he gifted it to them voluntarily.
ai.seo_question: Did women receive a share of war booty in early Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic distinction between the obligatory share (fay') reserved for combatants and the voluntary grant (nafala) given to non-combatant women who accompanied the Prophet’s army for nursing duties. Shia scholars utilize this narration to establish that women’s participation in war, even in support roles, warrants material compensation, though their legal status regarding booty distribution differs from that of the fighting men. This incident underscores the practical recognition of women’s contributions in early Islamic military campaigns as recorded in the foundational hadith collections.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, form Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, altogether from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said that

Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> went out with the women during the war until they would treat the wounded, and did not distribute for them anything from the war booty, but gifted it voluntarily for them’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn all from ‘Uthman from ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah from one of the two Imams, recipients of divine supreme covenant, who has said the following: “
The Messenger of Allah took part in war in company of women so that they could nurse the wounded. He did not give them a share of the captured properties but he did so in an optional manner.”
